title: Counting Window for Qualifying New Money on Savings and Money Market Accounts
content:
Qualifying new money on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is not always counted over the whole three-month window. Which window is used turns on the direct deposits credited to the owner's Personal Checking relationship and on how much new money the account itself took in most recently.

Two figures are read from the savings account's own records. The three-month total is the total of the deposits posted to the account in the three calendar months ending on the correction date other than internal transfers and automatic transfers from another Piedmont Crescent Bank account. The one-month new money is the same total taken over the one calendar month ending on that date. The third figure is read from the owner's Personal Checking account: the direct deposits credited to it in the three calendar months ending on the correction date.

### Condition, judgement, result

**Condition.** Direct deposits to the owner's Personal Checking account of at least 6000.00 USD in that three-month window, and one-month new money of at least 500.00 USD.
**Judgement.** The recent month stands for the whole window.
**Result.** Qualifying new money is the one-month new money grossed up by a factor of 3, rounded to the cent.

**Condition.** Direct deposits of at least 3000.00 USD but below 6000.00 USD in that window, and one-month new money of at least 500.00 USD.
**Judgement.** The recent month stands for the window only where it does not overstate what the account actually took in.
**Result.** Qualifying new money is the lesser of the three-month total and that same grossed-up one-month figure.

**Condition.** Direct deposits below 3000.00 USD, or one-month new money below 500.00 USD.
**Judgement.** The window is counted as it stands.
**Result.** Qualifying new money is the three-month total as posted.

### Boundaries and a worked case

Direct deposits of exactly 6000.00 USD fall in the first band; of exactly 3000.00 USD in the second; of 2999.99 USD in the third. One-month new money of exactly 500.00 USD satisfies its condition in the first two bands; 499.99 USD does not, and the three-month total then stands whatever the direct deposits were.

Take a hypothetical account whose three-month total is 9000.00 USD and whose one-month new money is 4000.00 USD, the owner's Personal Checking account having received 3500.00 USD of direct deposits in the window. The second band applies: the grossed-up figure is 4000.00 USD multiplied by 3, that is 12000.00 USD, and qualifying new money is the lesser of 9000.00 USD and 12000.00 USD, that is 9000.00 USD.
